newsitem.title: USA: Eurobonds get busier, IBM succeeds in dollars.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds get busier, IBM succeeds in dollars.

text.p: ** Primary market players were quick to pick up on the
perkier tone in U.S. Treasuries, with brisk activity
** IBM launched a warmly received $250 million three-year
deal at a 15 b.p. spread which tightened to 13/12 b.p.
** An AMEX unit set a $400 million five-year FRN.
** Korea Development Bank visited the market for the second
time this month, with a 500 million mark four-year FRN.
** Other deals spanned Canadian dollars, guilders, lire,

IBM set a $250 million two-year deal in early March through ABN AMRO Hoare Govett after a previous $250 million three-year, also via SBC Warburg at a 15 b.p. spread, in January. Both deals immediately tightened from their launch spreads.
American Express Credit Corp set a $400 million five-year FRN via Goldman Sachs International which said it was pleased with early sales.
"The pricing is a fair comparison with outstanding paper," a new issues manager at Goldman Sachs said.
The notes pay three-month LIBOR plus five b.p. and were reoffered at 99.782, a chunky discount to par by FRN standards.
Bayer Hypo set a C$100 million bond due December 1999 through itself and Toronto-Dominion. The notes, priced at 99.8475 with 1.375 points fees, were reoffered at 98.66 for a 15 b.p. spread.

A syndicate manager at TorDom said the deal was aimed at reinvestment flows from the hefty Canadian dollar redemptions due in May. According to Capital DATA Bondware, international bonds worth the equivalent of $1.13 billion mature in May, against a $725 million average in the first half of the year.
